 Anthony Gould (toe) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
 Gould is dealing with a toe injury and was listed as limited for the Colts’ first two practice reports of the week. He finished the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins and starts out limited, indicating he is in line to play Thursday against the Texans. Gould is suddenly the Colts’ starting slot receiver but should only be rostered in 14-team leagues with deep benches.
 -  Aditya Fuldeore

 Anthony Gould caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Colts’ Week 11 loss to the Texans. 
 Gould played sparingly despite the recent wide receiver departures, with his team-leading 48 yards more a statement on the current state of the offense than anything else. Nobody on this sinking team deserves fantasy consideration, a sentiment that extends to its depth pieces. 
 Anthony Gould 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 #6 
 Anthony Gould (toe) is active for Week 11 against the Texans. 
 Gould will play through his toe injury this evening, but he is on a boom-bust WR5. The Colts are playing without both of their starting offensive tackles, and Gould is not a replacement-level starter. 
 Anthony Gould 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 #6 
 Anthony Gould (toe) is questionable for Week 11 against the Texans. 
 Gould was upgraded to a full practice on Wednesday before receiving the questionable tag. We expect him to suit up tomorrow. He led the team with four targets last week, though Gould only turned that into two grabs for 28 yards. The Colts simply don’t have a wide receiver worth a look in even deep fantasy leagues. 
 Anthony Gould 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 #6 
 Anthony Gould caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins. 
 Gould operated as the Colts’ starting slot receiver, replacing Josh Downs. He led all Indy pass-catchers with a meager four targets, converting them into two receptions for 28 yards. Gould was shaken up after getting hit hard on a punt return, but he stayed in the game. The Colts’ pass-catchers don’t offer much fantasy upside but Gould is a desperation WR5 for Week 11 against the Texans. 
 Anthony Gould 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 #6 
 Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould will play slot receiver after Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs. 
 With Downs shipped out, the slot role will go to Gould, who has four receptions for 45 yards over three seasons with the Colts. Downs had accounted for 18 percent of the team’s targets and 24 percent of the team’s air yards through Week 9. The Colts use three wideout sets on 59 percent of their offensive plays, the 12th highest rate in the NFL. They rank 29th in EPA per pass attempt with three receivers on the field. Gould should be rostered in deeper formats based on route volume alone. 
 Anthony Gould 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 #6 
 Anthony Gould (concussion) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars. 
 The biggest news for fantasy purposes with the Colts inactives is simply that Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs are up, but that isn’t exactly surprising. Gould practiced in full the last two days of the week before being ruled out and stands a chance at being ready for Week 8. Inactive for the Colts are: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), TE Pharaoh Brown, DT Kevin Givens, T Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback) and CB Justin Walley (knee). 
 Sauce Gardner 
 IND 
 Cornerback 
 #1 
 Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings. 
 Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion). 
 Braden Smith 
 IND 
 Tackle 
 #72 
 Colts ruled out RT Braden Smith (concussion/neck) for Week 15 against the Seahawks. 
 The Colts will be without their starting right tackle for Sunday’s road game against a stout Seahawks defense. Backup Jalen Travis is expected to draw the start in his place and will be tasked with keeping one of either Riley Leonard or Philip Rivers upright. In addition to Smith, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (ankle) and CB Sauce Gardner (calf). 
 Adonai Mitchell 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 #10 
 WR Adonai Mitchell caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Colts’ preseason game against the Broncos. 
 Mitchell started in place of injured slot receiver Josh Downs (high-ankle sprain), though Mitchell was curiously subbed out for fellow rookie Anthony Gould on third downs, as noted by PFF’s Nathan Jahnke. Mitchell promisingly logged perimeter snaps opposite Alec Pierce in 12 personnel with the second-team offense. Gould averaged 22.0 yards per return on three total kickoff returns. 
 Anthony Gould 
 IND 
 Wide Receiver 
 The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Colts WR Anthony Gould could see starting snaps with Josh Downs (ankle) sidelined. 
 According to Boyd, Gould “has flashed more as a receiver than as a returner during camp.” The rookie fifth-rounder made a name for himself as a returner during his time at Oregon State, but with Downs sidelined for multiple weeks, there’s now a hole that needs to be filled at the slot position. Gould blazed a 4.39 40-yard dash at the combine this spring and totaled 44-711-2 in his final season of college. He played just 33.5 percent of his college snaps from the slot but had a 90.5 percent slot rate in 2021. We wouldn’t expect Gould to offer much fantasy upside, but this is worth monitoring as the team figures out a temporary replacement for Downs.

 Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful for Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.

This has, sadly, become pretty standard for Kincaid as he simply has to be managed week-to-week on the injury report.  Anthony Richardson 
 IND 
 Quarterback 
 #5 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson will start in Week 12 against the Giants.
 The surprising release of Daniel Jones immediately thrusts Richardson back into the QB1 role, a role he hasn’t held since 2024. The former No. 4 overall pick now has a chance to make the most of what is a lost season for the Colts, who are fresh off a 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Richardson has played sparingly this season, completing 2-of-4 passes for eight yards while rushing three times for six yards. Playing in an offense that’s devoid of weapons at receiver, the Colts would benefit from leaning into Richardson’s ability as an athlete by utilizing him in the ground game. Richardson’s rushing upside could eventually put him on the radar as a decent QB2, but we will conservatively project him as a low-end QB2/QB3 in his first start in over two years.
 -  Zachary Krueger 
 Source:  James Boyd

 Daniel Jones 
 FA 
 Quarterback 
 #17 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Colts waived QB Daniel Jones.
 Well, the Colts apparently evaluated everything, as they said they would last night. Wow. Jones makes it 11 games into a two-year, $88 million contract. He will be subject to waivers since the trade deadline has passed. It’s possible — though we’d be hard-pressed to say likely given the $2 million owed this season, $10 million next year and $38 million in non-guaranteed 2027 cash — that someone takes a chance on the deal. If not, he’ll be free to sign anywhere for the rest of the season. Minnesota would probably take a gamble on him again after they scooped him up in this same exact manner a few years ago, but that’s just speculation on our part. It’s stunning in the sense that it happened in-season, but this was obviously the way things had been trending as Indianapolis’ offense simply hasn’t been able to operate with Jones. Anthony Richardson will take over as the starting quarterback for the time being.
 -  Rivers McCown

 Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
 According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

 Rams head coach Sean McVay said “there is a possibility” Davante Adams (hamstring) plays in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
 The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported last week that the Rams were “hopeful” this would be the timeline for Adams’ return. McVay somewhat confirmed that optimism while speaking to the media on Friday, but noted that the star receiver isn’t “ready quite yet.” This follows McVay announcing that Puka Nacua (knee) will miss the next few months after MCL surgery, so it’s safe to assume the Rams will be thin at receiver in Week 12 when they take on the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

 Mayfield reportedly looked good in Friday’s practice and logged back-to-back practices to close out the week. We should have an update on his official game status soon, but all signs are pointing to him starting this week against a Lions team that has allowed the fifth-most passing yards this season.  Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was seen practicing on the side field on Friday.
 This will presumably result in a DNP for Tuten this week, but we’ll see what the team announces when it releases its final injury report. According to Jaguars beat writer Ryan O’Halloran, Tuten was on the field with his helmet to stretch with teammates during warmups but then went to the side field. If he is listed as a DNP, it would be the second straight day Tuten failed to get on the practice field, but he could still receive a questionable designation entering the weekend. We will check back in with a final status update once the team announces it in a few hours.
